chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayub, from Al-Husayn ibn 'Uthman, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who doubts while he is standing, not knowing whether he had performed Rukū' or not. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should perform Rukū' and perform Sajdah.'
ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they doubt whether they have bowed (ruku) while standing in prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi addresses the specific legal scenario of doubt (shakk) occurring while standing, where the worshipper is uncertain whether the ruku' (bowing) has been performed. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes a corrective action of performing the ruku' followed by the prostration (sujood), reflecting the Shia jurisprudential principle of resolving ambiguity through a specific remedial act rather than restarting the prayer. This ruling highlights the practical application of clarity in ritual worship, ensuring the validity of the prayer despite minor uncertainties in physical movements.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Al Husayn Bin Usman, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the man who doubted and he was standing, not knowing whether he had performed the Rukū or not. Heasws said: ‘He should perform Rukū and perform Sajdah’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from al-Husayn ibn ‘Uthman from ibn Muskan from abu Basir who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who in a standing position doubts and does not know if he has performed Ruku‘ (bowing down on one’s knees) or not. He (the Imam) said, ‘He performs Ruku‘ and Sajdah (prostration).”’
